editorial:
Imagine waking up in a strange place where everyone is stuck inside a giant urn. You can hear people talking a mile a minute, but the catch is that they are only talking to themselves. You never actually connect with anyone else. You get to follow a complicated love triangle featuring a husband, his wife, and his mistress. It feels like a weird dream where the rules of life have completely changed, and you are just trying to figure out why you are there and how to deal with the people you betrayed while you were alive.

The acting is top-notch and makes the weird setting feel real. You will love how the movie handles the tension between the three leads as they face their mistakes. The pace is a bit slow at times, but the strange visuals keep you interested. If you enjoy stories that make you think about life and death without being too heavy, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, the three main characters finally stop talking at themselves and actually listen to each other. They realize that their selfish choices in life led them to this lonely place. Once they truly forgive one another and admit their faults, the urns break open. They are finally freed from their isolation and allowed to move on to a peaceful afterlife together, proving that honesty is the only way out.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about the afterlife and human relationships.
